      "title": "isAccessTokenId matcher rejects matching grant shortcuts and checks the wrong prefix offset",
      "body": "In matchesSafely(), `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so every token with the expected grant shortcut is rejected. In addition, the 6-character prefix is laid out as session[0:2], token[2:4], grant[4:6], but substring(3,5) reads characters 3 and 4. The check should use substring(4,6) and return true when that equals expectedGrantShortcut. As written, the updated expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions will fail for valid issued tokens."

      "title": "Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId",
      "body": "The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, \"Null rawTokenId not allowed\")` for the rawTokenId parameter, so rawTokenId is never validated and the error message is misleading. If a caller supplies a null raw token id, encodeTokenId() will later produce a token id ending with `:null` instead of rejecting it, potentially breaking the expected uniqueness of jti. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, \"Null rawTokenId not allowed\")`."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 33,

      "title": "Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing grant type factories",
      "body": "`getShortcut()` is added to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default implementation. Existing third-party grant type factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement this method, causing `AbstractMethodError`/`NoSuchMethodError`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `getShortcut()` on every factory, so server startup or token issuance can fail after an upgrade. If this SPI is intended for extensions, the new method should be a default method or missing shortcuts should be handled explicitly."
    },

      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java",
      "line": 102,

      "title": "Public copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context",
      "body": "The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted from the public nested `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class. Extensions that copy an existing grant context will fail to compile or link after this change. If this removal is not intended as a breaking API change, keep the constructor and copy the newly added `grantType` field (`this.grantType = context.grantType`) as well."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 74,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Custom grant shortcuts with a length other than two produce unparseable token IDs",
      "body": "The default encoder and decoder hard-code a 6-character prefix composed of 2-char session type, 2-char token type, and 2-char grant type. `postInit()` validates only duplicate shortcuts, not their length, and `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not specify a 2-character contract. A custom grant type returning, for example, a 3-character shortcut will be accepted here and emitted in access-token IDs, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will later reject those IDs because `encodedContext.length()` is not 6 or because the grant substring is misaligned. Validate exactly two characters at startup or enforce/document the length contract."
    }

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher rejects matching grant shortcuts and checks the wrong prefix offset
findings.body: In matchesSafely(), `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so every token with the expected grant shortcut is rejected. In addition, the 6-character prefix is laid out as session[0:2], token[2:4], grant[4:6], but substring(3,5) reads characters 3 and 4. The check should use substring(4,6) and return true when that equals expectedGrantShortcut. As written, the updated expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions will fail for valid issued tokens.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` for the rawTokenId parameter, so rawTokenId is never validated and the error message is misleading. If a caller supplies a null raw token id, encodeTokenId() will later produce a token id ending with `:null` instead of rejecting it, potentially breaking the expected uniqueness of jti. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing grant type factories
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default implementation. Existing third-party grant type factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement this method, causing `AbstractMethodError`/`NoSuchMethodError`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `getShortcut()` on every factory, so server startup or token issuance can fail after an upgrade. If this SPI is intended for extensions, the new method should be a default method or missing shortcuts should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: Public copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context
findings.body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted from the public nested `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class. Extensions that copy an existing grant context will fail to compile or link after this change. If this removal is not intended as a breaking API change, keep the constructor and copy the newly added `grantType` field (`this.grantType = context.grantType`) as well.

findings.title: Custom grant shortcuts with a length other than two produce unparseable token IDs
findings.body: The default encoder and decoder hard-code a 6-character prefix composed of 2-char session type, 2-char token type, and 2-char grant type. `postInit()` validates only duplicate shortcuts, not their length, and `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not specify a 2-character contract. A custom grant type returning, for example, a 3-character shortcut will be accepted here and emitted in access-token IDs, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will later reject those IDs because `encodedContext.length()` is not 6 or because the grant substring is misaligned. Validate exactly two characters at startup or enforce/document the length contract.
